## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymized: authors' identities are hidden from reviewers and reviewers' from authors; the Editors know both (instructions copy dated 2026-05-07, https://web.archive.org/web/20260507171808/https://academic.oup.com/cje/pages/General_Instructions). Before review, all submissions go through a preliminary assessment carried out collectively by the editorial board at its regular meetings; papers that do not pass are not sent to review, for reasons the journal lists (see Framing Requirements). Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No transfer or cascade policy appears on the pages read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. Nothing on the pages read says so |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev reports 1.3 review rounds on average, n = 4 (https://scirev.org/journal/cambridge-journal-of-economics/), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Peer review results and the editors' own assessment are considered together by the editorial board, which makes the final decision collectively. An appeal route exists for papers rejected after peer review: one appeal per article, by letter to the Managing Editor, with evidence if a reviewer is said to have made technical errors; decisions on appeals are final, and the editors say they rarely reverse decisions (instructions copy, same URL, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, a "Use of AI" paragraph in the journal's own instructions (copy dated 2026-05-07, https://web.archive.org/web/20260507171808/https://academic.oup.com/cje/pages/General_Instructions) that points to the publisher's ethics page (not read) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with disclosure |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | AI language tools such as ChatGPT do not qualify as authors, and the publisher screens author lists for them. Use of AI, for example to help generate content or images, write code, process data or translate, must be disclosed both in the cover letter to the editors and in the Methods or Acknowledgments section. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://web.archive.org/web/20260507171808/https://academic.oup.com/cje/pages/General_Instructions |

## Format

> Source: the "Information for Authors" page, Wayback copy dated 2026-05-07 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260507171808/https://academic.oup.com/cje/pages/General_Instructions); the live page returns HTTP 403, so current wording may differ. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Articles; comments on articles published in the journal (normally no more than 1500 words, to be sent first to the original author with a request to respond to possible misunderstandings). The instructions do not list other types. OpenAlex type counts for 2021-2026: 325 articles, 4 paratext, 3 errata, 1 editorial, 1 book review, 1 letter |
| **Word limit** | Submissions should not normally exceed 10,000 words including tables and references |
| **Word limit negotiability** | "Not normally" is the journal's wording; no statement on how exceptions are granted. References and tables count inside the 10,000 |
| **Abstract limit** | Abstract of no more than 250 words, up to five keywords, three JEL classification codes and an address for correspondence; manuscripts should be suitably anonymised |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 10,000 words. Citations use the Harvard system of short references with an alphabetical list at the end; footnotes kept to a minimum, as superscript figures typed by hand, not the word processor's footnote feature |
| **Supplementary material** | Authors of accepted papers are encouraged to submit data sets, programs and information on the empirical analysis, published as supplementary data; not required, and not to be submitted where this would breach third-party rights or identify individuals |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables and figures go on separate sheets at the end of the manuscript; figures at least 300 DPI at final size; colour figures are free online and the charge for printed colour is GBP 350 per figure; alt text descriptions for all figures are required at submission |
| **Layout and style** | Double spaced, including footnotes and references; journal style (see a recent issue); funding sources must be named at submission |

### Orientation

> Counts in this section come from 335 OpenAlex records of 2021-2026, of which 330 carry an abstract (98.5%: article 323 of 325; by year 2021: 57 of 57, 2022: 63 of 65, 2023: 59 of 60, 2024: 48 of 49, 2025: 54 of 54, 2026: 49 of 50). Abstracts were rebuilt from OpenAlex's inverted index and each regex was tested on title plus abstract of those 330 records (patterns in the regex register in AI-Research Notes; names in code font below). Retrieved 2026-11-23. Caveat: the `conceptual_theory` regex includes the very broad word "theory" and over-states conceptual work; use `methodology` as the narrower measure.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Both appear. `conceptual_theory` 136 of 330 (41.2%), `model` 55 (16.7%), `formal_math` 16 (4.8%), against `empirical` 39 (11.8%), `econometric` 19 (5.8%), `survey_data` 15 (4.5%). The journal's own aims call for "the provision and use of empirical evidence" together with theoretical, applied, interdisciplinary, history-of-thought and methodological work (https://web.archive.org/web/20260507171808/https://academic.oup.com/cje/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Neither dominates by counts: `econometric` 5.8%, `survey_data` 4.5%, `experiment` 5 (1.5%), `qualitative` 7 (2.1%), `case_study` 8 (2.4%), `mixed_methods` 0. The instructions restrict mathematics and econometrics (see Framing Requirements) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The aims welcome contributions from heterodox economics "as well as other social science disciplines" (same instructions copy). Primary-topic counts above are economics-labelled throughout (Political Economy and Marxism 36, Housing, Finance, and Neoliberalism 20) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, stated by the journal. It runs on cooperative principles and assesses every paper collectively; papers are not sent to review if the editors feel they are "not sufficiently heterodox in orientation", too narrow in scope, do not add enough to existing debates, are outside scope, are insufficiently developed as an academic paper, or do not follow the journal's guidance on mathematics and econometrics. The editors regard decisions made on this preliminary assessment as final (instructions copy dated 2026-05-07, https://web.archive.org/web/20260507171808/https://academic.oup.com/cje/pages/General_Instructions). Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** The journal states a focus on theoretical, applied, interdisciplinary, history-of-thought and methodological work, with strong emphasis on realistic analysis, critical perspectives, the use of empirical evidence and the construction of policy, on issues such as unemployment, inflation, the organisation of production, distribution, class conflict, underdevelopment, globalisation, changing forms and boundaries of markets and planning, and uneven development and instability (same page).
- **Mathematics and econometrics**: authors are asked to use mathematics only where it does not compromise realistic analysis and econometrics only where essential to valid inference; neither is to be used merely to demonstrate technical expertise; the major steps must be intelligible to a non-mathematical reader, with the technical parts in an appendix (same page).
- **Article types**: articles and comments (same page); three open special-issue calls on the 2026-11-14 home copy (see Publication Frequency).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the preliminary assessment can end a submission before review, and its outcome is described as final (same page). No rate is published, and SciRev's four reviews do not state how many were stopped at this stage (https://scirev.org/journal/cambridge-journal-of-economics/).

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Blank. The instructions copy (2026-05-07) has no ethics-approval or human-subjects statement; it refers readers to the publisher's ethics page, which was not read (https://web.archive.org/web/20260507171808/https://academic.oup.com/cje/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author work is half of the output: 162 of 328 records with author lists (49.4%) (https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.issn:0309-166X,publication_year:2021-2026), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No affiliation or independent-scholar rule is stated in the instructions copy, which asks for an address for correspondence and an anonymised manuscript. Review is double-anonymized (Peer Review) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Encouraged for accepted papers (data sets and programs as supplementary data), not required; submitters must name funding sources (instructions copy dated 2026-05-07) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-anonymized review; manuscripts must be suitably anonymised; the Editors know authors' identities (instructions copy). Working papers in a series may be posted before acceptance and may stay online (Preprint Policy). The publisher allows the author's original version to be posted anywhere at any time (https://academic.oup.com/pages/self_archiving_policy_b, read from the Wayback copy of 2026-11-02, https://web.archive.org/web/20261102215712/https://academic.oup.com/pages/self_archiving_policy_b), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **AI use** | Disclosure required in the cover letter and in the Methods or Acknowledgments; AI cannot be an author (instructions copy dated 2026-05-07) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; an open access charge applies if chosen (amount not read); printed colour figures cost GBP 350 each; no submission fee is stated in the instructions copy. Authors exclusively license copyright to the Cambridge Political Economy Society and may reuse their own material non-commercially with acknowledgment (instructions copy) |
| **Appeals** | One appeal per article is possible after rejection following peer review, by letter to the Managing Editor (instructions copy) |

Per layer: OpenAlex counts (types, countries, topics, open-access status, authorship) 4; OpenAlex abstract-based keyword counts 4 (330 of 335 records have an abstract, 98.5%); the journal's own policy and format text 3 (Wayback copy dated 2026-05-07 of the instructions, so about six months old; live page 403); board and roster 2 (copy dated 2023-03-25; current roster unreadable); publisher-wide self-archiving policy read from the Wayback copy of 2026-11-02 (live page Cloudflare 403) 4; experiential layer 2 (SciRev n = 4; LetPub 0; nothing else).

The method-row scores use the pass's own thresholds stated under Methodological Preferences.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Orientation and scope**: every submission gets a collective preliminary assessment, and papers can be stopped before review for being too narrow, not sufficiently heterodox in orientation, not adding enough to existing debates, outside scope or insufficiently developed; the editors call these decisions final (Framing Requirements, Peer Review; instructions copy dated 2026-05-07).
- **Mathematics and econometrics**: a paper that does not follow the journal's guidance on their use can be stopped before review (Framing Requirements).
- **Length and format**: normally no more than 10,000 words including tables and references; an abstract of at most 250 words, up to five keywords and three JEL codes; an anonymised manuscript (Format).
- **Prior publication**: papers previously published elsewhere are not accepted, except in working-paper series where the series came before acceptance (Preprint Policy).
- **AI use**: undisclosed AI use breaches the disclosure rule (AI Policy).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; ethics-approval rules are unknown (Practical Concerns blank).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: no journal-published figure exists; SciRev's four reviews average 11.3 months for the first round and 13.3 months total for accepted papers (Review Cycle Time), a very small sample.
- **Preliminary assessment**: it is made collectively by the board at its regular meetings (Peer Review), with no published rate and no published turnaround for it.
- **Cost**: open access carries a charge of unknown size (Open Access); printed colour figures cost GBP 350 each (Format).
- **Technical content**: mathematics and econometrics must be explained for a non-specialist reader, with technical parts in an appendix (Framing Requirements).
- **Copyright**: authors exclusively license copyright to the Cambridge Political Economy Society and keep non-commercial reuse rights (Practical Concerns).

### Best Suited For

- Heterodox, Marxian, Post-Keynesian and institutional political economy: `marx_keynes_tradition` in 106 of 330 abstract-bearing records, "Political Economy and Marxism" as the third-largest primary topic (36), and the journal's stated tradition (Epistemological, Top Topics).
- Finance, financialisation, labour, class and development: `finance` 104, `class_labour` 82, `development_south` 76 of 330 (Sensitive Topics).
- History-of-thought and methodological work, which the aims name: `historical` 46 and `methodology` 47 of 330 (Methodological Preferences).
- Empirical work that keeps technique subordinate to realistic analysis: `empirical` 39 and `econometric` 19 of 330, with the journal's stated emphasis on empirical evidence and its rule on technique (Orientation, Framing Requirements).
- Single authors: 162 of 328 author lists are single-author (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Formal-model-heavy or technique-led papers: the instructions restrict mathematics and econometrics, and non-compliance can end a submission before review (Framing Requirements).
- Mainstream-orthodox framings without a critical angle: papers can be stopped for not being sufficiently heterodox (Framing Requirements); the counts do not show how often mainstream work is published.
- Experimental, mixed-methods or systematic-review designs: `experiment` 5, `mixed_methods` 0, `review_types` 0 of 330 (Methodological Preferences). Rare here, not shown to be rejected.
- Anyone who needs a fast or predictable turnaround: SciRev reports about 11 months for a first round (n = 4) and the journal publishes no figure (Review Cycle Time).
